_comment: The malfunction procedures for the failure catalog's caution lights (data/failures.json, slice 9a), in every mission's CSM checklist book after its flight's lists (ChecklistBook.load_default()). A failure opens its procedure as it comes. The launch vehicle's lights (slice 9d) get the launch aborts' procedure, from the CSM Apollo Operations Handbook's section 2.9 [adapted]. The simulator's own [adapted]: each light's meaning is the C&W table's (CSM Apollo Operations Handbook, SM2A-03-BLOCK II-(1), pp. 2.10-5 to 2.10-8) [published]; the actions are those the simulated systems have.

steps.text: CRYO PRESS: an O2 or H2 tank's pressure out of limits (the HUD's CRYO line)
MASTER ALARM - press
An O2 tank at zero: the fuel cells on its valve module fail next. CM POWER - EMER, the emergency power-down
Each fuel cell whose FC light comes on - off its buses (FC 1, FC 2, FC 3)
FC 1, 2 or 3: a fuel cell's flow, temperature or pH out of limits
MASTER ALARM - press
The failed cell - off its buses (its FC switch, MDC-3): the other two carry the load
MN BUS A and B above 26.25 V (no UNDERVOLT light); if not, CM POWER - EMER
FC BUS DISCONNECT: a transient tripped the fuel cells' overload sensors, FC 1 to 3 off their buses; the entry batteries carry the mains, under 26.25 V (MN BUS A and B UNDERVOLT)
MASTER ALARM - press
In the launch: on to staging on the batteries, the IU flying
At Houston's call: each FC switch OFF and back ON (MDC-3), its cell back on its buses
MN BUS A and B above 26.25 V: the UNDERVOLT lights out
SCE: the signal conditioning equipment's NORM supply lost; Houston's telemetry reads nonsense (the HUD's TM LOST). No light: Houston calls it
At Houston's "SCE to AUX": SCE PWR - AUX (MDC-3), the telemetry back

checklists.title: Malfunction: SM RCS A, B, C or D

steps.text: SM RCS A, B, C or D: a quad's secondary fuel pressure out of limits
MASTER ALARM - press
The quad's RCS QUAD switch - off (MDC-2): isolate it
Its axes on the quad opposite: pitch on A and C, yaw on B and D. The autopilot turns slower about them
CMC: the computer has failed. Its DSKY is dark and its autopilot stopped
MASTER ALARM - press
ATT SOURCE - SCS: the SCS holds the attitude
Before an SPS burn: SPS GMBL MOTORS PITCH 1 - START, release to ON
Before an SPS burn: SPS GMBL MOTORS YAW 1 - START, release to ON
Before an SPS burn: SPS GMBL MOTORS PITCH 2 - START, release to ON
Before an SPS burn: SPS GMBL MOTORS YAW 2 - START, release to ON
Houston's PADs from here: each burn on the SCS, turned to the PAD's R, P and Y on the FDAI's GDC angles, to the EMS's count of its DVC (EMS FUNCTION DV, THRUST ON)
ISS: the IMU has failed. NO ATT on the DSKY: the CMC has no attitude
MASTER ALARM - press
ATT SOURCE - SCS: the SCS holds the attitude
Before an SPS burn: SPS GMBL MOTORS PITCH 1 - START, release to ON
Before an SPS burn: SPS GMBL MOTORS YAW 1 - START, release to ON
Before an SPS burn: SPS GMBL MOTORS PITCH 2 - START, release to ON
Before an SPS burn: SPS GMBL MOTORS YAW 2 - START, release to ON
No coarse align, P51 or P52 brings the platform back: the burns on the SCS, to the EMS's count
ISS: a transient drove the platform's gimbals round; NO ATT on the DSKY, the CMC without an attitude
MASTER ALARM - press
In the launch: the IU flies on; the GDC and the SCS keep the attitude (FDAI on the GDC)
In orbit, at night: P51 (V37E 51E), a coarse align to the stars and two sightings; the platform back, the ISS light out
Houston's REFSMMAT uplink, then P52 option 1 to it
Docking probe: the capture latches didn't engage the drogue, and the probe came back out of it. No light
Close again at about 0.1 ft/s, the probe onto the drogue's centre, and hold +X on the THC at contact: the probe held in the drogue
PROBE RETRACT - press (MDC-2), +X held: the probe pulls the docking rings together, the ring latches fire about 5 s on: hard dock
+X off: the ring latches hold the vehicles
Main parachutes: one deflated, streaming at a fifth of its diameter, two good. No light: seen out of the window, or called by the recovery forces
Two mains bring the CM down at about 36 ft/s at the water, against three's 32: within the design. Nothing to do but brace for the harder impact
After Apollo 15, whose main the CM RCS's dump most probably burnt: land with the RCS propellants aboard, not dumped under the mains
GPI: one axis swinging about its trim on one servo loop, as Apollo 16's yaw on loop 2 did, 1 deg either way at 2.4 Hz; the axis steady on the other loop. No light: the TVC check shows it
SPS GIMBAL MOTORS (4) - OFF, the bad loop's first

The flight rules want all four servo loops for an SPS burn before the landing: no burn until Houston clears the loop. Apollo 16's was an open in its rate feedback, a limit cycle the engine can fly with, the thrust damping it; it flew its burns on the primary loops, the secondary yaw motor on only to back them up

checklists.title: Malfunction: LV ENG, LV RATE or LV GUID

steps.text: LV ENG, LV RATE or LV GUID: a launch vehicle engine out, the vehicle's rates past the EDS's limits, or the IU's guidance lost
With the tower on and EDS AUTO: two S-IC engines out, or the rates, abort on their own, and the tower pulls the CM away (mode I)
One engine out and the rest burning, as Apollo 13's S-II centre engine at 5:30: no abort; the IU burns the others longer and steers on to orbit
ABORT light or Houston's 'Abort': the translation controller's handle - counterclockwise
Mode I: the canards at 11 s, then the tower's jettison and the chutes as the ELS brings them
Modes II to IV: the CSM leaves the launch vehicle 3 s after the handle; the handle back at neutral ends the SM's +X jets
Mode II: CM/SM SEP, lift up; ELS LOGIC and ELS AUTO on
Mode III: Houston's PAD, the SPS's retrograde burn (P40); CM/SM SEP; half lift, rolled 60 degrees to the south; ELS LOGIC and ELS AUTO on
Mode IV: Houston's PAD, the SPS's burn into orbit (P40)
